From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Capacity coverage heatmap + next steps (pipeline-linked reserve asks)

Team — attaching the Q2 coverage heatmap and the latest pipeline CSV. I built a quick view that maps committed/reservation needs against likely conversion weeks; highlights are in the PNG. High-level asks: 1) confirm whether we should recommend a reserved capacity ask to Nimbus (DEAL-8392) for a pilot month, 2) identify runway gaps between expected convert dates and our current Dedicated pool, and 3) propose mitigations (burst credits, cross-region routing, delaying non-critical rollouts).

Quick notes from the heatmap: we have a 6-week coverage gap if three mid-funnel deals convert on the earlier end (see rows highlighted red). If all convert on the later end, we have a 2-week cushion.

Attachments: coverage_heatmap_q2_v2.png (image), pipeline_forecast_by_deal.csv (csv)

Can each of you reply with a single-line decision and, where relevant, the delta we should push to finance for a short-term reserve? I want to consolidate responses before Monday's fleet planning call.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Fleet Strategy, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity coverage heatmap + next steps (pipeline-linked reserve asks)

Soojin — quick update from pipeline side. Three deals that drive the red rows are: Nimbus Cloud (pilot -> expansion), Meridian Health (POC), and Orion Analytics (proof-of-value). Nimbus is the one most likely to convert in the 6–8 week window; Jared (copied below on next thread) is targeting an early-May start for the pilot but could accelerate to late-April if we can promise a short burst of reserved capacity.

Recommendation: ask finance for a one-month reserved commit equivalent to ~200 GPU-months for Nimbus as a pilot. I'll confirm the exact timelines with Jared today and report back.

-Karthik
Principal Account Executive

Thanks — I pulled the attachments and ran a quick cost model. See attached cost_model_q2_spend.xlsx for two scenarios (conservative / accelerated convert). Short answers to asks: 

- If we proceed with a 200 GPU-month trial for Nimbus, finance needs a signed Statement of Work or a billing commit by the deal owner before we shift dedicated pool allocation. That buy-in moves the reservation from 'possible' to 'committed' in our monthly ledger.
- Estimated incremental cost (gross) for one month at 200 GPU-months: ~$98k before discounts; net depends on the discount schedule and any burst credits we apply.
- For runway gaps longer than 4 weeks we should formally propose a small temporary re-route policy to lower-cost regions (APAC/US-west) rather than over-provisioning.

Action for Karthik: when you confirm exact start weeks from Jared, please upload the signed SOW or at minimum a DocuSign intent link into the HubSpot record (I added the link field in related_links). Finance will triage once the link is present.

-Laura
Director, Finance Ops

Soojin / Team — thanks for the thorough breakdown and context. Quick answers: 1) We are aiming for the week of May 10 for the pilot kick-off (leads want early-May but engineering prefers the buffer), 2) Yes, Nimbus can sign a 1-month SOW for the pilot; legal is good with a short-form SOW, expect DocuSign next week, 3) We would like you to provision burst credits as a fallback in case initial load spikes beyond the pilot bucket.

We'll plan for 200 GPU-months for month 1 and will aim to convert to a 6-month reservation if KPIs hit agreed thresholds. Karthik / Soojin — please confirm the thresholds we will measure (latency P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens) and I'll ensure Nimbus' SRE has the runbook.

Regards,
Jared Martin
Head of Cloud Platform, Nimbus Cloud
jared@nimbuscloud.com
